chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily the companion of evil infects, and an evil associate destroys — so look carefully at whom you associate with.'

key_terms.تُقَارِنُ: you associate with — from qarana, meaning to pair, join, or become a companion to someone
key_terms.صَاحِبَ الشَّرِّ: companion of evil — one who habitually engages in wrongdoing
key_terms.قَرِينَ السَّوْءِ: evil associate/bad companion — a close intimate whose wickedness endangers others
key_terms.يُرْدِي: destroys/leads to ruin — from radiya, meaning to fall into destruction or perdition
key_terms.يُعْدِي: infects/contagiates — literally used of disease transmission, here applied metaphorically to moral corruption

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ridha say about the danger of keeping bad company in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a saying attributed to the Prophet Isa (Jesus, peace be upon him), reported through Imam Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), warning that the company of an evil person is morally contagious and that a corrupt companion can bring one to ruin. The teaching underscores the critical importance of choosing one's associates wisely, as moral corruption spreads through proximity and social bonds. This wisdom, shared across the Abrahamic traditions, is here placed by the Imam in an ethical framework particularly pertinent to the social environment of early Islamic society.
